Having adorned his own body with extensive ornaments, perfumes, and the like,
the reciter should chant the mantra according to the prescribed rite for the sake of attaining all accomplishments.
One should perform only a single ritual action while reciting [the mantra] day and night;
for the second [action], the form is said by the Lotus-born One to be fickle.
Beginning with the *praṇava* (oṃ), followed by the pair of *lajjā* (hrīḥ hrīḥ),
then the word ending in the vocative case, and finally joined with *māyā* (hūṃ), *phaṭ*, and *svāhā*, this [mantra] bestows the fruits of the four aims of life.
This knowledge must never be revealed, even at the cost of one's life;
its form is blue in color and endowed with all the Tantras.
Śrī Pārvatī said:
I desire to hear about all those deities, meters, and Ṛks, along with their respective colors; please tell me out of your grace.
The Lord said: O Goddess of the gods, having thus prostrated before Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara, I shall speak according to the prescribed rite; listen and be attentive.
In the syllable *va* is Varuṇa himself; in the syllable *ja* is the enemy of the gods (Viṣṇu);
in the syllable *ai* is the goddess Tripurā; and in the syllable *ra* is Tripurasundarī.
The goddess Trailokyavijayā is eternally established as the extraction [of the mantra];
Mahādeva is in the syllable *i*, and Girināyaka is in the syllable *na*.
In the vowel *ī* is Kamalā herself, and in the letter *ma* is Sarasvatī;
in the mouth of *ma* is the Great Goddess Prakṛti, the bestower of all accomplishments.
Vikṛti resides in the syllable *phaṭ*, and Kusumāyudha in *svā*;
Rati resides in *hā*, and Lakṣmī through the application of the *śrī* seed-syllable.
In the seed-syllable of modesty (lajjābīja), the one known as Māyā is Manobhavā;
in the fourth, however, is Guṇātītā, who bestows the knowledge of liberation.
The meter is Samrāt, the deity is Bhairava, and the sage is Mantrasamuccaya.
Now I shall proclaim the hymn which was composed by Brahmā in ancient times;
listen to that, O Maheśānī, for it is a ritual procedure difficult even for the gods to obtain.
At the navel is a white lotus, above which is a lotus and the mandala of the fierce-rayed sun;
she who is the sole essence of saṃsāra, the mother of the three worlds, and the source of the arising of dharma—
on that path, on the triple path, I bow to that Chinnamastā, the auspicious one who bears a triple body.
The Yoginī Yoganidrā, whose nature is wisdom and who removes the fear of death.
At her navel is a white lotus; her face shines with a bandhūka flower as red as the dawn;
on her left [hand] she holds a severed head, and in her other hand a large sacrificial knife (kartṛkā);
she stands in the pratyālīḍha posture, her garment reaching to the ends of the quarters, her mass of hair disheveled, while her own Śiva has been cut down.
Drinking the supreme [nectar] from which streams of blood gush forth.

She shines with three eyes that gleam with a radiance equal to the sun at dawn; she is fierce in form, holding a skull-ornament aloft from which streams of blood flow profusely from a channel other than the left,
and she holds a glittering flaying-knife in her lotus-like hand.
The red one with slightly reddened hair, free from vomiting, the colored one—his own power.

She stands in the *pratyālīḍha* posture, with the radiance of the tips of her armlets shimmering across the quarters of the sky; she is clothed in the directions, her hair reaches up to her head, and she is fierce and of terrible form like a mass of clouds at the time of universal dissolution.
She has a mouth with formidable fangs and speaks with the brilliance of a flickering tongue that shines like the best of suns.
Her pair of eyes flicker like lightning, and her formidable form rests upon the slope of my heart.
She who constantly nourishes the Ḍākinī with blood flowing from her severed throat,
whose lotus feet are indeed worshipped by Brahmā, Īśāna, Acyuta, and others, and who is incessantly meditated upon at every step by the foremost yogis who possess self-knowledge— [to her I bow].
I bow to her who is the form of thought,
the essence of saṃsāra, the mother of the three worlds, the praised Chinnamastā; I bow to that Yoginī, the form of knowledge, the sleep of yoga, who removes the fear of death.
With my mind, I contemplate her who bestows the desired and the undesired, who removes the impurities of the Kali age, and who assumes a threefold body to effect the creation,

maintenance, and dissolution of the world; she who, through the three qualities (*tri-guṇya*), becomes Brahmā, Hari, and the Wielder of the Trident— her, the primordial Prakṛti, who is my own transformation.
I remember [this] with my mind for the sake of accomplishing all goals.

(She, whose pair of smiling lotus-feet the immortals constantly worship)—I am intent on the worship of the union of the letters *ali* and *pisi*; I am sustained by the commencement of many kinds of streams of water;
I am detached from the world of ordinary people; I have entered into Bhairavī; I am devoted to the feet of the Guru; I am Bhairava.
I am the head.
This hymn of great merit was spoken by Brahmā in the past;
it directly bestows all accomplishments and destroys even the most heinous sins.
Whoever recites this upon rising in the morning, or even while remaining in the presence of the Goddess,
shall achieve the fulfillment of all aims, whatever dwells within his mind.
Wealth, grain, sons, a wife, a destroyer of enemies,
land, and great knowledge— these eight perfections shall surely be attained.
Furthermore, whatever else has been desired, all that [is obtained] through his grace.
Thus ends the hymn to Pracaṇḍacaṇḍikā in the Viśvasāra Tantra.
I shall describe the Prāṇāgnihotra, which is supremely pleasing to the Goddess.
For the sake of success, one should prepare ghee with milk in a bronze vessel.

One should scatter [the offerings] with the Astra-mantra and remove [impurities] with the Vahni-sundarī-mantra; having recited the mantra eight times, one should perform the drying, burning, and cooking [of the offerings].

Then, touching [the offerings] with the left thumb and transforming them into nectar with the Dhenu-mudrā, one should worship the root-mantra according to its respective form, ending in the feminine suffix -ī, followed by the Vahni-sundarī.

Again, having joined the palms in *añjali* and brought a flower to the face, one should display the *grāsamudrā* with the left hand and offer: "O Sovereign of the Gods, I offer this to you; please accept it.
Then, one should display the *prāṇa-mudrā* and others with the right hand.
The little finger, the ring finger, and the thumb [are used] with the words "To Prāṇa, Svāhā."
One should utter the word for *apāna* with the index, middle, and thumb fingers;
one should utter the word for *udāna* with the little, ring, and middle fingers, along with the thumb.
The middle, index, and ring fingers are for the instruction on increase;
one should also utter the word "equal" (samāni) from all the fingers.
Salutation to the two Bhuvaneśvarīs who are the supreme self. Thus.
Having again offered water for sipping (ācamanīya) and so forth, having performed the Agnihotra sacrifice with that same [substance],

having given betel-leaf (tāmbūla) and the like, and having presented incense and lamps, having displayed the parasol, chowries, and other [regalia], having performed the dedication of the ritual act (karmārpaṇa), and having prostrated, one should give the remains of the offerings (nirmālya) and so forth to the Vaiṣṇava attendants and experience supreme bliss.
One should partake of the great prasāda.
The entire Mahākālamata has been narrated by the Lotus-born One.
I bow to the supreme Bhavānī, the consort of Hara, who removes the terrible fear of Bhīma.
I bow to the primordial, supreme Mother of all beings, whose blue-hued breast is pressed by her son,
who is filled with streams of blood from the heads dripping from his own arm.
Salutations to you, the Mother of all, the supreme Śakti whose form is the syllable Oṃ; she who is adorned with a beautiful necklace of radiant skulls held in her right hand,
whose nature is bliss, whose face is half-filled with blood, and who holds her own head in her left hand, O Bhavānī.
Salutations always to her who possesses hundreds of thousands of auspicious marks, whose lotus feet are worshipped by gods and demons;
who is on the right side, composed of letters, possessing extremely sharp rays, red, wonderful, supreme;
who is naked, honored by the gods, smiling with happiness—to that goddess of letters, salutations indeed!
Salutations to you, O Goddess, who are worshipped by all the hundreds of hosts of gods,
who are most formidable, adorned with red ornaments, and who madden the entire multitude of bound souls (paśus).
You are the primordial power of the form of the dark, indeterminate *kalā*, [worshipped] by the gods headed by Brahmā.

To that Goddess Chinnamastā—the knowledge adored by the gods, who is Hari, Hara, and the immeasurable Śrī Bhavānī; who is eternal bliss, the remover of all fear, whose very nature is the form of Brahman; who is the embodiment of Time and the auspicious one—I bow.
Homage, homage to you, the Mother of all, who is indeed the form of Oṃkāra, whose face is like a thunderbolt,
who utters the syllable Hūṃ,
and who has pulverized the foremost of the Daityas with the sounds of Hūṃ.

Homage, homage to you, Bhavānī, the creator of all worlds, whose every direction is filled with the sound of "huṃ," who moves entirely by the sound of "huṃ," and who flows forth from the sound of "huṃ."
Salutations to you, the primordial one; victory to you of terrible form! Homage be to you, O Goddess, the supreme and the transcendent.
Salutations again and again to the power that is the prowess of Śambhu, and salutations to you who are established as that very power.
You are the Goddess worshipped by the gods, the remover of fear, the beloved of Śambhu, and the source of joy.

O Mother, you who are the primordial Śambhuparākramā, served by Hari, Hara, Brahmā, and the rest; you who are the Great Abode (Mahālaya) consisting of all forms, the Lioness (Siṃhī) possessing both aspects, and the one who is the very essence of the devotees—those who worship you, the first Siddhas and those yet to be perfected, [attain their goal]. O Brahmanī! You who are the primordial power of Śambhu’s prowess, served by Hari, Hara, Brahmā, and the others; you who are the Great Abode (Mahālaya) consisting of all forms, the Lioness (Siṃhī) possessing both aspects, and the one who is the very essence of the devotees—those who worship you, the first Siddhas and those yet to be perfected, [attain their goal]. O Mother! You who are the primordial Śambhuparākramā, served by Hari, Hara, Brahmā, and the others; you who are the Great Abode (Mahālaya) consisting of all forms, the Lioness (Siṃhī) possessing both aspects, and the one who is the very essence of the devotees—those who worship you, the first Siddhas and those yet to be perfected, [attain their goal]. O Brahmanī! You who are the primordial power of Śambhu’s prowess, served by Hari, Hara, Brahmā, and the others; you who are the Great Abode (Mahālaya) consisting of all forms, the Lioness (Siṃhī) possessing both aspects, and the one who is the very essence of the devotees—those who worship you, the first Siddhas and those yet to be perfected, [attain their goal]. O Mother! You who are the primordial Śambhuparākramā, served by Hari, Hara, Brahmā, and the others; you who are the Great Abode (Mahālaya) consisting of all forms, the Lioness (Siṃhī) possessing both aspects, and the one who is the very essence of the devotees—those who worship you, the first Siddhas and those yet to be perfected, [attain their goal]. O Brahmanī! O Mother! O Mother! You who are the primordial Śambhuparākramā, served

I bow to you, O Śrīmad Bhavānī, the supreme mother of all worlds— the one whose feet are worshipped by the assembly of gods, who is formidable and most terrifying, who is endowed with the totality of all the digits of bliss, who is eternally exultant, and who bestows grace upon the practitioner.
Homage to the Goddess Caṇḍā, the uniquely fierce Pracaṇḍā! Homage to the Goddess Durgā, who is truly Bhavānī!
Those who constantly praise her with a devoted heart shall have no fear of the intense terror of fever or affliction.
Jayā is of fierce form, Pracaṇḍā is exceedingly fierce, and she is Bhavānī, the ocean of the heart, whose form is spiritual perfection.
For those who constantly praise, recite, and remember [you], there shall be no fever, torment, or fierce fear.
O Goddess Umā, Durgā, you who are the supreme form of perfection, the supreme Ḍākinī, Varṇinī, the Mother of the Universe;
you who occupy half the body of Hara—protect this lamp! Homage to you, homage to you, homage to you, O Durgā!
O Lord of treasures, men have taken refuge in you; by your grace, the lords of men among men [have attained their status].
Having disregarded any other refuge, they have sought shelter at your pair of feet; therefore, purify these men with your favor.
The Goddess of the Universe praises You, the Sovereign, with hymns of praise doubled by the eight [syllables].
Blessed is he who brings all happiness upon the surface of the earth; in his home there is constant festivity.
He attains perfection, becomes the lord of all people, a skilled poet, eloquent, endowed with knowledge, and achieves both liberation and worldly enjoyment.
They are worshipped by all beings in the world, just as the lords of the gods are.
Thus ends the King of Hymns to Kauśikī, the Supreme Deity, in the Viśvasāra Tantra.
Śrī Pārvatī said:
"Salutations to you, O Lord, O Blessed One, who are the auspicious form of Śivā."
He who has assumed many forms for the sake of Śrī [Lakṣmī] provides the essence of success to those possessed of knowledge.

Salutations to You, who are Nara, who possess the form of a man, whose sole nature is the Supreme Self, the omniscient one, the source from whom all distinctions arise, and the mass of pure consciousness.
Salutations to Śiva, who is independent and whose form is eternally manifest, and who,
being dependent upon his devotees, bestows his grace upon those who are worthy.
To the one who brings about discernment for those seeking discernment, deliberation for those capable of deliberation,
illumination for those who illuminate, and the very form of knowledge for the wise.
One should offer salutations from the front, from both sides, and from behind; may there never be the opposite. Grant me your state of servitude, which is always and truly your own essential nature.
The Lord said: Now, O Maheśānī, I shall describe the eternal Śrī, who bestows all perfections;
by the mere mention of whom one obtains the four aims of life that are so difficult to attain.
The Sovereign Goddess said to the Lord of Gods: "O Lord, tell me truly the entire power of that eternal goddess whose head is bowed."
O Destroyer of Tripura, formerly on the beautiful mountain Kailāsa you spoke;
O Ocean of Compassion, reveal all of that to me this very day.
Īśvara said: "O Goddess, among the millions of tantras, these two are indeed the secret leaders of all mantras. Listen now to their armor (*kavaca*), which grants all desires."
O Great Goddess, I shall declare to you the supreme secret, the great and ultimate state of profound sleep,
which brings about all accomplishments for mantras.
Having first uttered the syllable Oṃ for the sake of accomplishing the mantra,
the practitioner of mantra should perform the recitation with his whole being here, day and night.
A person need not perform worship or ritual adoration of her; one should merely recite the mantra.
Then all supernatural powers, such as *aṇimā* and the rest, which are mines of excellent qualities, will be held in the palm of one's hand.

Oṃ: For these two mantras of Chinnamastā, the Seer (ṛṣi) is the Blessed Śiva, the metre (chandas) is Anuṣṭubh, the deity (devatā) is the primordial Power, the Blessed Goddess Chinnamastā; the application (viniyoga) is for the sake of the attainment of my own skill in poetry and scholarship.
May Oṃ protect my head; may Hrīḥ always protect my face.
May Vajravairocanī protect my throat and my heart at all times.
Huṃ! May Haripriyā protect the secret organ; huṃ! may she protect the back.
Phaṭ svāhā! May she protect the two sides, as well as the hands and the feet.
May Vijayā be at the region of the navel; may Jayā protect the two ears;
may Kavitvadā protect the cheeks; and may Parājitā protect the crest-lock.
May Bhavānī, the bestower of all sovereignty, protect [me] in the home;
may the Goddess Sarasvatī, devoted to the gift of knowledge, protect my mouth.
May Bhairavī, known as Siddhā, protect [me] at Rājasthāna during the worship of the gods;
may she who takes the form of Bhīma always protect [me] in the cremation ground, removing all fear.
O Goddess of gods, may you, who are the embodiment of existence and the remover of fear, protect my sons in the study of scriptures,
in debate, in battle, in water, and on the pure mountain.
May Jayā Śrī-Chinnamastakā protect me always in the forest;
may Caṇḍikā grant me protection from head to foot.
May the Goddess of the gods, who possesses a fierce form and dispels fear, protect my wife—
she who is the embodiment of eternal bliss and is established in all the Vedas.
O Great Goddess, may she who is eternally the source of auspicious power protect me always;
may the Ḍākinī Varṇinī grant me protection at all times.
"In the terrible, inaccessible, and fearsome abode of spirits and ghosts"—
thus, O Goddess, is this armor of yours, which is difficult to obtain in the three worlds.
This must not be spoken here or there, nor ever at any time;
it is concealed in all tantras, yet revealed in the Viśvasāra.
Listen to that, O Maheśānī; O beloved, these are prohibited for those who have not mastered the restraints (yama).
O Maheśānī, by giving [these] to them, the siddhis are destroyed in due course.
O beloved, one should not give this armor to one who is deceitful, devoid of devotion, cruel, a slanderer, greedy, or wicked.
O beloved, this armor should be given to a disciple who is endowed with devotion, possessed of great aspiration, auspicious, a Vaiṣṇava, and pure.
O Goddess, by the mere remembrance of this armor-mantra (kavaca), one obtains the fruit of the four aims of life;
yet, O Great-Souled One, I cannot describe the power of this armor even in hundreds of years.
O Maheśānī, I am unable to describe its fruit;
it is not for wives, nor for sons, nor for kinsmen, O Pārvatī.
They do not see sorrow, and they become worthy of honor by kings;
having become pure, whether already pure or otherwise, [they obtain] the armor that fulfills all desires.
A mortal who is capable of reciting or even remembering [this] shall become a sovereign lord named Ānandanandasindhu, a preeminent poet, and one who is immune to curses and malefic planets.
Such a mortal becomes a master of all speech, honored by the world, and a lord of wealth;
in battle, among spirits, and in debate, his victory shall be certain.
A mortal endowed with sons and grandsons, a man of pleasure for all women,
shall have his enemies reduced to servitude and remain forever beloved by everyone.
Proud and hunchbacked, the disputant stumbles at the mere sight of him;
even death becomes a deity, and he is a servant to that lord of the earth.
O Goddess, this secret, difficult even for the gods to obtain, has been told as an incidental matter;
having received the grace of the Guru, one obtains this well-guarded Vidyā.
Even there, O Goddess, this armor is difficult to obtain within the three worlds;
the Guru is the god Hara himself, and his wife is the beloved of Hara.
For one who worships without making distinctions, success is not far off.
The practices of mantra have been explained previously; one should recite them while honoring them in their proper sequence.
One should contemplate the light at the navel and likewise the face in the heart;
such a man becomes a master of great speech, possessing sovereignty and the ability for excellent poetry.
O Great Goddess, a mortal who constantly engages in union with women there and is devoted to the fivefold conduct becomes a perfected one; it is not otherwise.
One endowed with power should recite the mantra; one should not recite the mantra alone.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, and those gods who are the best of the immortals—
Seeing that practitioner, O Goddess, they praise him filled with joy.
Thus, O Goddess, this armor (kavaca) of Caṇḍādevī has been proclaimed to you.
Having approached and propitiated this Guru, who is the manifest embodiment of the wish-fulfilling tree and the direct bestower of devotion and liberation,
no person is deluded by ignorance or pride, nor do they succumb to dullness.
He is indeed perfected; truly, they go to the further shore of all sufferings and calamities.
O Goddess, for him there is constant prosperity, and his enemies are destroyed;
one should wear this written [mantra] on the hand, or on the neck, or on the head, or on the arm.
O Maheśvarī, whatever is in one's mind shall be accomplished for that person if [this] is written on birch bark with gorocanā and saffron.
For him, there are no successes or failures, nor any fear of the world of suffering anywhere;
he is a speaker who nourishes liberation, and the lord of the earth remains indifferent toward him.
Pride is humbled, crookedness is straightened, and even the lord of the earth becomes cool like fire;
for in his hand rests the supreme eightfold accomplishment of conduct, which brings about the eightfold perfection.
I bow to that Gaurī, beloved of the Lord of the Mountains, who shatters the fear of worldly existence.
Thus ends the *Pracaṇḍacaṇḍikā-kavaca* from the *Viśvasāra-tantra*. The Lord said:
Having risen early in the morning and having purified one’s hands and feet, [one should...]
Facing north, one should perform a prostration to the guru with devotion.
Whether by mind, by speech, or especially by bodily actions,
[one should worship] Kṣetrapati, Vāsturāja, and thereafter Vighnarāja.
One should always bow to Durgā, Vināyaka, Śambhu, Bhairava accompanied by Vaṭuka, as well as Brahmā, Nairṛta, and Cakrapāṇi.
One should always bow to the obstacles, to the lords of obstacles, and even to the sages.
Having thus prostrated, O Goddess of the gods, the wise man should meditate upon the Goddess.
Whether in a wilderness, a cremation ground, a deserted dwelling, or likewise in a house,
one should cultivate the realization of non-duality, regarding the body as being like the entire universe.
Having meditated upon the foundational power (Ādhāraśakti) who holds two lotuses,
one should then contemplate Janārdana in the form of a tortoise upon her head, O Goddess.
One should contemplate with the intellect the god who resembles a dark blue cloud and is endowed with all principles, and the god Ananta situated upon his back.
One should meditate upon the ploughshare, endowed with a thousand hoods and resembling pure crystal, on the portion of the hump, and the mallet on the left side.
Adorned with the jewel of a single earring as his supreme ornament,
one should indeed contemplate the earth situated upon the Single-Wheeled [City] with the intellect.
Likewise, for the sake of accomplishment on the earth, the wise one should meditate upon her thus:
as white rice-grains of black color, adorned by a pair of earths.
It was filled with hosts of various virtues and populated by all sentient beings;
it was strewn with mountains and rivers and adorned with every kind of jewel.
The goddess who consists of all mantras, the enchanting consort of Viṣṇu,
who is filled with oceans and rivers, and who is manifested at all times.
Here too, one should mentally visualize a pavilion adorned with jewels;
then, [one should visualize] a wish-fulfilling tree (kalpavṛkṣa) there, which grants the fruits of all desires.
And that great lion-throne of yours, established in that state,
is a seat endowed with dharma and other virtues, and possessed of all knowledge.
Adorned at the gateway in the four directions with figures such as Karāla,
it is endowed with various paintings and embellished with diverse jewels.

One should meditate according to this procedure upon [the deity] endowed with various limbs and weapons, adorned with the syllable *oṃ* and so forth, and equipped with the sacrificial ladle (*sruk*), sword (*khaḍga*), and other implements.
The wise one should always contemplate the bulb of bliss (ānandakanda) upon its head;
there, consciousness is the stalk, endowed with all knowledge.
Having meditated there upon that which is joined with all the beginningless [principles] and adorned with the three mandalas,
one should likewise contemplate an eight-petaled lotus together with its pericarp.
Having meditated upon her as multicolored, adorned, and exceedingly beautiful—
thus having contemplated with the mind the Goddess of the Suras residing within the heart-lotus.
One should meditate according to this method as spoken by Śaṅkara;
one should contemplate Rati and Kāma engaged in inverted sexual union.
Upon her back, one should contemplate the Goddess in the form of Mūlaprakṛti,
namely Ḍākinī, joined with Varṇinī on the left and right sides respectively.
The goddess has a skull and a knife in her hands, is adorned with a garland of severed heads,
wears a necklace of bones, and has a serpent as her sacred thread.

I ever meditate with devotion in my heart upon Bhavānī, whose lotus feet are worshipped by gods, asuras, and others; she who holds her own head in her left hand and a sharp, formidable scythe in her right hand on her right side.

I bow to that primordial goddess, whose two feet are worshipped by the gods and sages, who stands in the *pratyālīḍha* posture, who agitates and subdues the three worlds, who is eternal, who dwells within the three cities (*tripura*), whose very nature is the destruction of the afflictions of the three realms, and who consists of thirty [deities].
Salutations always and eternally to her whose lips are the universe and whose feet pacify all sins.
Establish me in Your mind, which abides as the Self of all beings; O Great Goddess, may this pair of Your feet bring peace.
Day by day, for my sake, grant Your approval; You are the Power residing within my life-breath, the giver of fear to those who oppose You.
I bow;
O Mother, I bow eternally to that third step of yours, which is beyond comprehension and destroys evil fortune.
For the sake of the cause worshipped by gods and asuras, I perpetually praise that which is the source of all that is attained.
O Bhavānī, bestow upon me, your servant, that gaze which is the essence of the hearts of all friends, which subdues the entire flood of worldly existence,
and which spreads an eternal light that dispels all thought of the body.
Salutations to you, the abode of majesty, the pure one who lasts through age after age until the end of time, the pacifier of Time.
Salutations to you, salutations to you, the destroyer of the world at its end, whose form is the very nature of existence.
O Enemy of Tripura, you are the root of your own lineage, the fierce trident that destroys the calamity of Time.
You are Brāhmī and you are Raudrī; you are the one praised by Hari and Hara, known as Parā and Bhavānī.

You are the eternal Nityā, the form of Time, the remover of all fear, and that which is supreme among all vidyās. You are Gaurī and Chinnamastā, the destroyer of the impurities of the Kali age; you are the river known as the Ocean.

You are the Mother, you are Tāṇḍa, the progenitor of the three worlds; you are the form of Time (Kāla) to your enemies. You are Kālī, the consort of Śambhu, praised by Hari and Hara; you are Bhadrakālī, Karālī, she known as Pretā, whose form is that of a ghost, who holds a lotus in her hand, who is the embodiment of the noose, and who is the Supreme (Parā).
I remember You, the primordial Prakṛti, with my mind for the sake of attaining the ocean of stars (the firmament).

O Mother, even from afar, a father [seeks] the one who instantly pacifies the fear of worldly existence for his sons. O Mother, there is a longing for Your grace even for those whose very selves are the far shore of the ocean of saṃsāra.
Having constantly abandoned that [state], you have reached completion; O Goddess, do not place me within your own lineage, for you are not Surā (wine), but Surāri (the enemy of the gods).
You are Parā (the Supreme), you are Purā (the Ancient), you are Ratī (Delight), and you are Surāri (the enemy of the gods).
You are night, you are day; you are the poor, you are the wealthy; you are the happy one, you are the creator of sorrows, and you are the wielder of swords.
O Mother, save me—you who are the supreme savior of heroes and whose necklace consists of boundless skulls.
O you whose power is playful accomplishment, O excellent one, youthful, mature, and dwelling in Vṛndāvana;
O sleep, drowsiness, sport, O Halā, Kālā, Kālī, of terrible roar;
salutations to you, salutations to you, salutations be to you, O Durgā; salutations to you, O Bhavānī, this is the truth.
Salutations to you, salutations to you, O you who are the perfection of compassion; salutations to you, salutations to you, she who is the supreme Ḍākinī.

Your garland of bones is conceived by the wise to be like fragrant flowers belonging to the enemy of the gods (Śiva). With your severed head, may you strike down [the enemy]; that which is called Devapadma has been proclaimed by me as an offering.
Since your head rests upon your own arm, that very head is indeed the one praised by the lords of sages.
Furthermore, they who know the Vedas declare that what is your own right [hand] is then made yours by you;
that which is your *varṇinī* (the colored one), the *ḍākinī* and consort of Hara, is on the left, while that [head] is on the right.
O Brāhmī, whose feet are worshipped by the hosts of gods; likewise, O Kṛṣṇā Vaiṣṇavī;
you, O Goddess, have attained a state of being worshipped by the hosts of gods through your contentment.
Having set forth toward you, O Bhavasundarī, daughter of the mountain, may there be auspicious peace from the foot of the Lord Śaṅkara.
The Mother who deludes the world, who removes all fear and bestows both security and prosperity—
those two who formerly stood near Hari,
joined as a pair by Śambhu and Śambokā, lull the universe to sleep.
Having attained this state honored by the hosts of gods through contentment, we depart for Bhavasundarī; O Daughter of the Mountain, salutations to the Lord of Prosperity!
O Mother, worshipped like the lotus petal, within that limited inner circle—
Her form resembles a wheel and a womb, worshipped by the wives of gods and asuras; for a moment, I constantly praise and bow to the consort of Hara for the attainment of the fruit of peace.
Grant satisfaction to the gods and brahmins, O bestower of sacrifice, for the sake of the desired prosperity equal to Lakṣmī.
You are Śrī, you are Īśvarī, Buddhi, Lajjā, Lakṣmī, and Sarasvatī; you are Śānti, Jayadā, Nityā, Ambā, and likewise Kṣemaṅkarī;
you are Brāhmī, Māheśvarī, Gaurī, Karālī, and Vikarālinī.
She is Satī, the devoted wife, the virtuous, the beautiful, and the beauty of the city; she is the nature of consciousness, the auspicious one, Gītā, Gaṅgā, Sītā, and Sarasvatī;
she is the Goddess consisting of all mantras, the bestower of the fruit of all peace.
O beloved, you are indeed the very nature of water, the all-pervading sovereign composed of all mantras;

this eternal Vasundharā stands here upon the earth through your peaceful power. Without her, how could there be stability or the performance of pacification rites on this ground, since in the past Satī was provoked to anger?
The power in water is always proclaimed by the sages to be of the nature of taste; in the sphere of fire, it is of the nature of burning; and in that wind, it is of the nature of touch.
In the ether you are sound and form; subtle, you possess a subtle nature.
On earth you are the full power, as declared by the Lotus-born One.
The goddess is described by the Lotus-born One as being tender, mature, youthful, and bestowing aesthetic delight, and as consisting of all powers.
You are Lakṣmī, residing in the seed-syllable of Lakṣmī; you are Lajjā, the Sovereign of the World (Bhuvaneśvarī);
you are Māyā, the sprout from the seed-syllable, eternal, and the destroyer of the fear of worldly existence.
Sarasvatī resides in the syllable *vā* [of Vāgbhava]; Vāruṇī is situated in the syllable *va*;
the Mother of the Worlds is in the syllable *ja*; and Vimalā is established in the syllable *vai*.
The syllable *ra* is the pacifier of all sins, the beautiful goddess of fire;
and the syllable *ca* is the goddess Caṇḍikā, the destroyer of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa.
Nārāyaṇī is to be known in the syllable *nī*, and Citsvarūpiṇī in the syllable *kā*; Brahmāṇī and Vaiṣṇavī are to be known in the syllable *ca*, and Parameśvarī in the syllable *ra*.
Phaṭkāra is the bestower of fruits, and Śambhusundarī resides in Svākāra;
the Self is Ardhanārīśvara, and Haravallabhā resides in Hākāra.
O beloved of the Day-maker (the Sun), these Mātṛkās, who abide in the castes and were fashioned by Brahmā ending with the syllable 'Brahman', must always be honored and praised.

O Mother, that power of His, which is an indescribable majesty here, purifies Viṣṇu—who performs all tasks in the world—constantly for the sake of the intentions of every heart; purify Your devotees in the cause of attaining the fruit [of liberation].
O Mother, by propitiating your pair of feet, even Brahmā and the others,
as well as other sages and gods mentioned in the Vedas, the Bhāgavata, and so forth, shall possess an imperishable fame.
Satisfied by the words of Vedānta, you are adorned by the words of Vedānta;
I eternally bow to her who abides in the abode of Śiva, she who is supreme and transcendent through the words of Vedānta.
You are Kālī, the form of Time, the pacifier of the fear of worldly existence, the Death of Death, the Terrifying One.
You are lofty, you possess a lofty form; with your gurgling sound, you are of terrible aspect, yet endowed with compassion and other virtues.
You are eternal, of eternal form, the pacifier of the fear of worldly existence, the embodiment of yoga, and the source of the ages;
you are the nature of consciousness and the form of fire—remove all that is of the nature of defect within the ocean of existence.
You are Śivā, eternally sharing half the body of Śiva; you are the supreme Śivā, the Ḍākinī, and the source of the universe.

O Lord of Sages, through the yoga of devotion, you are the eternal and ever-perfect refuge for the sages. You are forbearance, you are the creative power (kalā), and you are the form of Time (Kāla). You are Śivā, the sanctuary and the sustainer of the all-pervading lords.
Sovereignty;
the state of being a master among masters, divinity among gods, and the essence of essences—O possessor of enemies, purify me!
You are the fulfiller of all aims, the thought, the flickering, the impetuous, and the moving one.
The goddess consists of all powers; she is eternally present as the daughter of the mountain.
You are Caṇḍā, of fierce form, with a flickering body, the creator of the subtle essence;
you are Svāhā, the embodiment of power, saluted by the best of gods, whose nature is the syllable Drīḥ.
You are the primordial one, the universal form, this very earth honored as the moat surrounding the excellent chariot of Varuṇa.
I bow to you, whose nature is existence, who are saluted by Hari and Hara, and who grant success to those seeking perfection.
You are the source of the Vedas, possessing the body of the *praṇava*, the embodiment of Brahman, and Bhavānī.
You are worthy of worship, the one to be adored, and the eternal remover of all fears for practitioners.
In the syllable *Oṃ*, you are Bhavānī in the form of the letters, the sustainer of the three worlds through the form of the letters;
you are eternal, of venerable form, the upholder of the most subtle, and the mistress of the wind of the Vedas.
You are the treasure of treasures, always white in color; you are the essence of all arts, always fair in hue.
Afflicted by hunger, for hunger indeed torments; with the essence of essences, purify those who are thus tormented.
Having placed your foot upon my body, grant that which is always desired in the heart.
Salutations to You, who, for the sake of attaining peace from my worldly transformations,
manifest the universe as Your own body according to the scriptures;
I bow to You, the eternal witness, with devotion through my mind and likewise through my physical actions.
Therefore, she is eternally blessed; she who is censured as "blessed," yet possesses feet that move with a *khilakila* gait;
she who is supreme in her steps, known by another name, ever meditative, encircled by the sound of *kilikilā*, fallen, and dense with discipline.
O Beloved, those whose ears do not hear this Vidyā— which is swift-footed, which sings forth your qualities, and which arises from your virtues—
and those whose hands do not perform your worship, O Dear One— [their lives are in vain].
O lotus-faced one, you must go to the place where his feet are to be found for that purpose.
O Goddess of the gods, salutations always, salutations again and again to those sages;
salutations to them, salutations to them, salutations to them, salutations again and again.
Salutations, salutations to you, the creator of all worlds; salutations, salutations to you, the progenitor of the universes.
Homage, homage to those whose prowess is Śambhu; homage, homage to the Goddess known as the Supreme and the Non-supreme.
The dispute among the people of the world regarding the form of their abodes has been described by the wives of the Enemy of Smara (Śiva) as being of subtle nature;
for those whose strength is overcome by passion, a messenger sent by amorous young women is appropriate.
O auspicious lady, for him who praises her every day with even fifty verses, prosperity dwells in his home, as do the powers beginning with *aṇimā*, which are mines of all virtues.
He who daily praises the Goddess in due order with hymns of the Krama system,
all women shall come under his control and he shall become an abode of prosperity.
In the entire world, there exists no hymn equal to this.
Thus ends the *Krama-stotra* of the supreme goddess Pracaṇḍacaṇḍikā in the venerable *Viśvasāra-tantra*.
Having praised him according to the prescribed rite, one should then instruct him in breath control (prāṇāyāma);
therein, the various types of prāṇāyāma were described by the Lotus-born One (Brahmā).
The embodied practitioner should perform the offering of oneself with this mantra;
having joined the palms in añjali, one should recite this mantra.
Prior to this, due to its authority over the functions of the vital breath, intellect, body, and dharma,
it undergoes the states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep.
Then one should proclaim: "By mind, by speech, and by action," and likewise, "by the feet, with magnanimity," again and again.
Whatever is done with wood and whatever state is remembered,
may it all be an offering to Brahman, accompanied by the syllable Om and the word "namas."
Śrī Pārvatī said:
You have truly related the thousand-name hymn (sahasranāmastotra) of the Pracaṇḍacaṇḍikā-vidyā as previously mentioned, which is esteemed by all.
On the delightful peak of Kailāsa, endowed with various minerals,
that best of mountains frequented by hosts of Siddhas and Gandharvas.
Seated amidst a thicket of various trees, enveloped by sprays of water droplets,
he sat with a joyful lotus-face due to his meditative absorption and ascetic penance.
The destroyer of the pride of enemies, three-eyed, bearing a spear,
endowed with a mass of matted hair, three-eyed, and having the sun as his essence.
Served by various Vedas and Shastras, it was as cool as the moon;
fair-complexioned like the luster of the moon, it was accompanied by various rhythmic beats.
The Goddess questioned Giriśa, Śiva, the soul of all beings,
regarding the majesty of the goddess Caṇḍikā, which is difficult even for the gods to attain.
The Lord of Gods spoke exactly as he had been told by Brahmā in the past;
having heard those words of his, the Lord of the World laughed.
He related all of that which had emerged from the Brahma-vajra;
O Pārvatī, listen to the majesty of the goddess Pracaṇḍacaṇḍikā.
In her everything has arisen, in her it still abides today,
and into her this entire world of moving and unmoving things will go to its dissolution.
For she, O beloved, brings all this forth from her own womb;
Kāla, Māyā, Kalā, and the Ātman—all these are established within her.
In her, I was born in former times, endowed with all the principles (tattvas).
From meditation upon her, there arises the praise of the world, followed again by salutation in due order.
O Goddess of the Gods, for her there is no mortality—no birth or death—in age after age; hear now of her power according to this method.
At dawn, at midnight, and during both twilights, he who recites this is the best of practitioners; he indeed is the illustrious Sadāśiva himself.

For this hymn of the thousand names of Pracaṇḍacaṇḍikā, the venerable Śrī Sadāśiva is the seer (ṛṣi), the Samrāṭ is the meter (chandaḥ), and the goddess Pracaṇḍacaṇḍikā— the primordial power (ādyā śaktiḥ) whose nature is the self-power (ātma-śakti) of the Blessed Lady— is the deity (devatā).
My application (viniyoga) is for the attainment of the fruits of the four aims of human life.
Having meditated upon that Goddess in the form previously described, one should always recite this hymn of praise.
Oṃ! Pracaṇḍacaṇḍikā, Caṇḍī, Caṇḍarūpā, Satīsakhī, Aticaṇḍā, Mahācaṇḍā, Kālarātri, Vasundharā.
Mahāmāyā, of terrible form, free from sorrow, the destroyer of grief;
Kātyāyanī, the Mother of the World, the Mother of the Universe, devoted to her husband.
Honored by the world, the life-force of the universe, the destroyer of fierce evil,
blissful, truthful, free from greed, resonant with the sound of flowing rivers, and most auspicious.
Muktadeśī, Sukeśī, Ghorā, Gharghararūpiṇī,
Visannā, Vipannā, Svacchatpannā, and Pativratā.
Ghoranetrā, Viśālākṣī, Kāmākhyā, Kulasundarī,
Kusumā, Mahākāmā, Vinodā, and Sarvasiddhidā.
She has three eyes and blood-red eyes; she is three-eyed and squint-eyed in form.
She is grey-haired, fond of raw flesh, the mother of the aged, and devoted to her husband.
The good lord, the true lord, the truthful one who causes agitation in the assembly;
she whose love is peerless, whose love is great, whose love is supreme, and whose very essence is love.
Kālākṣī, Kālarātri, Ghoranetrā, Ghṛṇā, Kṛpā, Sutṛptā, Svātṛptā, Ahalyā, and Pāpanāśinī.
She with squinting eyes, she of noble lineage, well-born, and honored by her family;
she who is broad, worthy of protection, delightful through devotion, and eternal.
She is the pure-faced one, the beautiful-faced one, the one with a flickering tongue, and she whose gait is graceful;
she is the woman, the moving one, the restless one, and the destroyer of various asuras.
She is the form of sound, the syllable Oṃ, and the form of the syllables Hrīṃ;
she is the seed-syllable of Śrī, the embodiment of modesty, the wrathful one, and the broad-hipped woman.
She whose seat is a corpse, who dwells on funeral pyres and shrines, who loves sacred trees, she who is auspicious;
she who is Chinnamastā, the destroyer of pride, the one of perfect mind, and the embodiment of mantra.
She has eyes like hollows, lotus-eyes, deer-like eyes, and gazelle-like eyes;
she is the fierce one, the fickle one, the unsteady one, the restless one, and she who loves the restless.
Capalāṅgī, Capalā, Karmapāśāhikā, Kṛmi, Kṛpāvatī, Kṛpā, Indrākṣī, and Haravallabhā.
Nārāyaṇī, Viśvamātā, Bhavānī, Pāpanāśinī,
Cāmuṇḍā, Ugracaṇḍā, Mahācaṇḍā, Umā, and Uṣā.
She is the wisdom-knowledge, the great knowledge, the knower of knowledge, and the destroyer of ignorance;
she is the giver of knowledge, the one whose knowledge has increased, and she whose form is the seed-syllable of the six groups.
She is of corresponding form, of vast form, of essential form, yet devoid of form;
she is both formless and of essential form, devoted solely to the true Dharma.
She is Sandhyā, Sandhyā, and Suśīlā; she is the embodiment of truth and dharma. She is the gentle Śālagrāma stone, the resident of Śālagrāma.
The entire hall and assembly, as well as the beautiful-breasted woman in the form of breasts, have vanished; life has departed from the wish-fulfilling cow, who was equal in every art.
Uneven and disjoined, yet perfectly joined and appearing as union;
she who brings about creation, maintenance, and destruction; Vārāhī, whose body is like a boar.
She is the lioness-form of Nṛsiṃha, the consort of Ramā, the beloved of Vāmadeva, whose body is slender;
she has a throat like that of a peacock, a neck like a conch-shell, beautiful arms, and the form of a graceful neck.
Kabandhā, Kabandhā, Kṛtvī, the destroyer of all rites,
Rādhikā, Satyabhāmā, Bālikā, and she who has the form of a child.
Suvahā, Suraṅgā, Vivāhū, Vāhūrupiṇī,
Dīrghabāhū, as well as Kharvā, Kharvadehā, and Vināvatī.
Danturā, Sudatī, Bhīkṣā, Yugadantā, Yugāvatī,
Sudantā, Vidantā, Atidantā, and Mahāmatī.
She who has one tusk, one fang, and terrible fangs; she who is the sun and the moon;
she whose essence is the sun, the wife of the sun, and who resides within the solar disc.
The limit of the sky’s expansion, the calamity, the uneven course;
the Sun, the digit of the Sun, the son of the Sun, the twelve-fold one, the maker of day.
Bhānu, Subhānu, Svarbhānu, Bhānurūpā,
Bharīduti, Tapanī, Tāpinī, Dhūmrā, Marīci, Jvālinī, and Ruci.
Sunandā, Bhogadā, Viśvabodhinī, Dhāriṇī, Kṣamā, Pūrṇā,
Pūrṇāmṛtā, Candrā, Ardhacandrā, and Aticandrikā.
She who dwells within the lunar orb, she who is ever possessed of the moon, the beloved;
she whose essence is the moon, she who possesses the luster of the moon, the moonlight, the goddess Śrī, Prīti, and Aṅgadā.
Pūrṇā, Pūrṇāmṛtā, Toyā, Tuṣṭi, Puṣṭi, Rati,
Dhṛti, Śaśinī, Candrikā, Kānti, Sarvakāntā, and Nivāsinī.
Abiding in the center of the lunar disc, she is the bestower of desires and born of the gods;
she is the self, the intellect, the great intellect, the intellect of all, and the upholder of excellent intellect.
She who is the self of all and the mother of all, who possesses every form of conduct,
whose very nature is truth and dharma, and who causes agitation within the assembly.
Ignorance (avidyā) consists of both the positive (vidhi) and negative (rūpa) forms; it takes the form of knowledge (jñāna), illusion (māyā), and the mountain-like (acalākṛti).
Through consciousness (cit), the non-conscious (aciti) becomes the principles of the self-sense (ātma-buddhi), ego (ahaṅkāra), and mind (manas).
She is both conceivable and inconceivable, immeasurable, and established in the true reality;
she is the form of the seed, the form of the living soul, and the embodiment of all seeds.
Viriṇī, Reṇukā, Kumbhā, Sukumbhā, and Śubhāmatī; Kṛśāṅgī, Kulīśāṅgī, Vajrāṅgī, and Vajrasambhavā.
Vṛkṣaśobhā, Suśobhā, Viśobhā, Viśabhaprabhā,
Pāṇḍavā, Dhūmravarṇā, Raktavarṇā, Rati, and Smṛti.
She is white in color, with white limbs, white, and of a white hue;

She is Kālī, the one who removes the afflictions of the lineage, the destroyer of all afflictions;
she is the giver of delight, the love of Rati, the auspicious bestower of joy to both gods and asuras.
The maiden was blessed, honored, possessing celestial chariots, and full of pride;
she was stout, tall, exceedingly tall, with long eyes and auspicious marks.
The Yamunā is always abundant, overflowing, fragrant, the refuge of women, possessing various forms, truthful, and youthful.
Yaśodā, Gati, Yajñā, Yādavī, Vanavāsinī,
Vanamālinī, Vipakhyā, Viśeṣākhyā, and Ratipriyā.
Yajñā possesses manifold virtues; Jñānā indeed destroys ignorance;
Dhī, Dhṛti, Rasā, Alomā, Lomasī, and Sulomasā.
Possessing manifold forms, she is delightful; she is the destroyer of form and the bestower of form.
She is the one who shapes, the one who is perished, the one who is perfected, and the great withdrawal.
Candrānanā is to be known as the first, the sovereign of the three worlds;
Duritā, Kulapūjyā, Mātaṅgī, and Kulasundarī.

Sarvāṅgasundarī, Nityā, and likewise Tripurasundarī;
Āryā, Dvaipāyanī, Kṛṣṇā, Virūpā, and Vipācikā.
Ṣaḍgarbhā, Nahāgartā, Premaprītā, Ramāvatī, Suśīlā, Puṇyaśīlā, and the honored Śāmbhavī.

Aparṇā, Niścalā, Lolā, Sarvanityā, Nagātmajā, Kairātī, Ārokṣasī, Ghorā, Ugratārā, and Sarasvatī.

Manā, Mantravidyā, Mahāvidyā, Mahāmantrā, and Mahāmahā.

Citralekhā, Sulekhā, Lekhā, and Priyadāyinī.

she holds a serpent-noose, is black in color, and has hair as red as blood.
She is the smoke-flame, the female corpse-eater, the moon; she dwells in corpses and carries corpses.
She wears a garland of bones, she is the bone itself, she is without bone, and she reviles the Vedas.
The Mother of the Vedas, the Crest of the Vedas, Viśākhā, she who dwells upon the peacock;
the Goddess who bears various musical sounds, who awakens the bow and the shield.

they sit in the hero’s posture (vīrāsana), drink the drink of heroes (vīrapāna), and likewise always drink meat.
She who delights in wine, who has a taste for meat, who bestows joy, whose name is Joy;
she who is Totalā, Tulasī, Tuṇḍā, and the dweller within the syllables of Tuṇḍa.
She should be meditated upon as having the form of the support, dwelling in the *mūlādhāra*;
she possesses manifold splendor, is moist, is embraced by Rudra, and is broad at the base.

she is known as Kalā, honored by Time, and she who sports at all times.
She is Mahākālā, whose form is Time (Kāla), and who possesses the forms of Paramākhya and others;
she has the mouth of Pāvanī, is the Vedas, and is expansive with all branches of knowledge.

adorned with pride and ornaments, she is auspicious, bearing various weapons.
She is Sarvāṇī, she is all the junctions of time, she is the triple junction, the embodiment of Time;

Ambā, Ambālikā, and Ambā; the great Ambikādrūdinī;

she is the Gītā, the Gāyatrī, and the Sāvitrī who brings an end to hell.
Revatī, Rohiṇī, Cetā, and Cintāsarvavināśinī;
these are the twenty-seven Ṛk-stems, belonging to Kaśyapa and dear to Kaśyapa.
Mṛtsnā, Sulā, Mālā, Sarvamālā, Mahatprabhā,
Pretadehakarā, Jyeṣṭhīvālā, Raudrī, and Bhrāmarī.

Haridvārāvatī, Tīrthā, Mathurā, and likewise Dvārakā;
Avantī, Aṅgadā, Pampā, Vicitrā, and Vibhramā as well.
Svapnāvatī, Haṃsamukhī, Lopāmudrā, Subhadrikā,
Śvetāruṇā, Bheruṇḍā, and Uttarā Kulasundarī.
Bhairavī, whose body is vast, resides within the bodies of enemies;

Haṃsākhyā, Valākā, Kākasya, Avikaṭānanā, Pubhratā, Puṣpahāsyā, Supuṣpā, and Puṣpahāsinī.
She is the wavering one, the delusive one, she who dwells in all stages of life;

Śakuntalā, Devayānī, Putrikā, Apsarā,
Gopālikā, Nadī, Indrā, Vikaṭā, and Kaṭapūtanā.
The goddess Tripurā Bhairavī, who embodies the fifth lunar day,
dwells upon all mountains and resides in the cremation ground.
Consisting of all the Vedas, she dwells at the gates of both heaven and non-heaven;
she is the eighth and ninth lunar days, as well as the new moon and the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight.

all these are the dissolution of all seasons, bringing about the end of even the most perfect kalpas.
She is all maidens, the mother of all, the truth of all, the virtuous one, and the child;
she is Kuntī, she is skillful play, and the destroyer of Śambhu’s pride.

she who brings joy to Hālāhala, Kālīkā, and the destroyer of Durga.

Aruṇākṣī, Candramukhī, Sarvanāmī, Sarasvatī,
she who is the form of the Śruti and Smṛti, and she who delights in the scriptures of ritual action.

the one who brought about the end of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, the messenger of Śiva, and the beloved of Śiva.
